items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: I mean it would depend on what year was Cecil Taylor talking about, and how popular was Dave compared to Cecil at that moment.

ctx.x: Well he might have been. I mean in terms of that sort of stuff though, he had Joe Glaser, who was, you know, Louis Armstrong’s manager. Joe was a very firm business guy. He knew those guys were in demand and he pretty much would take everything to the limit of what he could get from a club owner or whatever. And he kind of knew what those limits were. Whereas I think a lot of times, I know for myself over the years I’ve called places and usually you never get a call back, you know that whole story. And then it’s…

And also to get into your question more precisely I mean it would depend on what year was Cecil Taylor talking about, and how popular was Dave compared to Cecil at that moment. I mean it could be a completely color blind issue. You know Dave had maybe already had “Take Five” as an international hit and probably Cecil Taylor, and I’m just saying that because no one’s had a big international hit that you could find on a juke box. Like it wouldn’t matter if Cecil Taylor was God himself, that would be the business…
Yeah, how many people are going to come and see this person?
